title: Correctness probability under Hamming closeness
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S,A\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, and let $\delta\in\mathbb{R}$. If the relative Hamming distance from $f$ to the parity function indexed by $A$ is at most $\delta$, then the uniform probability over $y\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$ that the local correction of $z\mapsto f(\phi(z))$, at $x=\phi^{-1}(s_S)$ and $y$, equals the parity function indexed by $A$ evaluated at $s_S$ is at least $1-2\delta$. Here $\phi$ is the coordinatewise binary-to-sign bijection and $s_S$ is $-1$ on $S$ and $1$ off $S$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps the sign cube of dimension $n$ to the sign set
